reviewed_version: arXiv:2503.14699v2, 54-page author manuscript; exact version visible in PDF and arXiv metadata; journal-version equivalence not established
inspection_outcome: Initial scientific completion with two Major core-derivation findings and three Minor finding groups; explicit bounded repairs and counterevidence recorded.
summary: Support/cutoff claims fail as written and a Fourier family disproves the A-uniform semigroup derivative estimate. Corrected choices can restore these steps. Three local groups concern heat endpoints/kernel scaling, a time-integral comparison, and initial-data homogeneity of the energy bound. The main theorem is not established false.

problems.title: Support scales and recursive cutoff containments in critical initial data
problems.location: Definition3.1 pp14–15; Lemma3.3 pp15–17; Definition3.4 p17; Proposition3.7 pp19–21; Remark3.12 p23
problems.claim: Support envelopes shrink, amplitude lower bounds hold, and χk+1=1 on mollifiedψk support gives common initial data.
problems.assumptions: Fixedδ0, arbitrarily largeA, Mk-periodic nonempty supports; exact stated cutoff plateau and convolution radius.
problems.check: Fixedδ0 neighborhoods fill torus atMk>sqrt(3)π/δ0. Printed bump fails on intervening annulus; new-pipe plateau andx=xj evaluation do not follow. ExactNash algebra yieldsPdiv(χ²Dψ).
problems.result: Literal support-decay claim false and core containments not supplied even after scale correction.
problems.impact: Directly affects BMO data, amplitude recursion and common trace; not a proof that mainnonuniqueness isfalse.
problems.correction: Useρk=δ0/Mk, enlarged majorant, explicit cumulative transition/mollifier cutoff construction, periodic-corrector local-volume induction and scaled-axis phase selection.
problems.counterevidence: Separationformula alreadycontainsMk^-1. Full bounded compatible repair retained and checked; actualsupport nesting unnecessary onceenvelopesnest.

independent_acceptance.decisive_reasoning: Nonempty Mk-periodic supports have covering radius at most sqrt(3)pi/Mk, so a fixed positive physical neighborhood fills the torus at large A and cannot satisfy shrinking volume. The printed bump cannot majorize the larger annulus. The supplied plateau before convolution does not cover its enlarged support, and exact amplitude squaring gives P div(chi_(k+1)^2 D psi_k), not the displayed single-power identity.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: Checked rho_m=delta0/Mm, cumulative transition widths d_(m,k)=rho_m*2^(-(k-m+2)) and a_(m,k+1)=a_(m,k)+d_(m,k)+ell_k. Old supports after convolution lie on every next plateau; the new support uses ell_k<rho_k. Total transition plus mollification width stays below rho_m/2, and sum_m d_(m,k)^-1 is O(M_(k-1)), giving uniform derivative bounds. Enlarged periodic majorants and the local corrector induction preserve local volumes. Scaled-axis grid points, followed by an O(Nk^-1) phase adjustment inside the old ball, give the amplitude lower bound; uniform base estimates avoid an A-dependent initial-data loop.
independent_acceptance.impact: The false literal supports and missing containments affect BMO initial data, amplitude recursion and common trace. The repaired finite chain does not certify an entire revised paper or refute the main theorem.

problems.title: False A-uniform Holder-gradient evolution estimate
problems.claim: Weighted derivative bound withoutt^-κ/2, uniform inlargeA.
problems.check: Y normO1, projected divergenceexplicitFouriermode; heat/claimedboundratioL31/32. Equation3.19givesactualdrift exponentiallysmall e^-cL34; C1κDuhamel comparisonpreserveslowerbound. Nativecountercheckagrees.
problems.correction: Retain t^-κ/2; choose0<κ<min(α,1/2−1/(2γ)−2α). Betaintegral andsameXnorm thenclose, withgradientgain(α−κ)/2.

independent_acceptance.hypotheses: alpha=1/32,b=6,gamma=2,kappa=1/16,epsilon=1/64 are allowed; the original kappa upper bound is 3/16. A=L^17,N0=L^34,n=L^16,s=L^-34,t=L^-32 use integral frequencies.
independent_acceptance.decisive_reasoning: The time-localized symmetric tensor has Y norm uniformly bounded because sqrt(s)*n^(1+kappa)=1. Its projected divergence is the explicit transverse Fourier mode. The heat weighted-gradient/claimed-bound ratio is n^(kappa(1-2epsilon))=L^(31/32). On [s,t], N0^2*s=L^34, so the source's actual-drift derivative bounds are exponentially small; C^(1,kappa) Duhamel comparison cannot cancel the surviving heat mode. The counterexample concerns the stated A-uniform constant, not all fixed-A constants.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: The source proof gives the weaker gradient estimate with t^(-kappa/2). The beta integral is finite for epsilon<alpha, and after multiplication by the existing X gradient weight the gain is t^((alpha-kappa)/2). Choosing 0<kappa<min(alpha,1/2-1/(2gamma)-2alpha) closes both self-map and contraction; this interval is nonempty before choosing A. The trace argument retains its required C1 interpolation.
independent_acceptance.impact: The stated stronger bound is a used core perturbation estimate; its valid weaker replacement and restricted kappa choice are recorded separately.

problems.title: Local heat endpoint scope and kernel spatial scaling

independent_acceptance.decisive_reasoning: For f_J=sum_{j<=J}2^-j sin(2^j x), the source Zygmund C1 norm stays bounded while the derivative of heat evolution at t=4^-J and x=0 is at least J/e. The claimed zero-gap output-Linfinity upgrade therefore fails. Separately the annular multiplier at t=0 has inverse transform N^3 check(pi)(Nx), disproving the printed unscaled pointwise kernel bound.
independent_acceptance.repair_and_impact: A positive smoothing gap or summable Besov input repairs the endpoint. Restoring N^3 and N|x| restores uniform kernel L1 control. No failure of the traced positive-gap operator uses is established.

problems.title: Vanishing small-time comparison for a positive integral

independent_acceptance.decisive_reasoning: For fixed A and t2=1 the k=0 positive integral has a strictly positive limit as t1 decreases to zero, whereas the printed positive power of t1 tends to zero. The full Gamma integral bounds III by sqrt(pi)*sum Nk^(1+beta1)/N_(k+1), uniformly convergent because 1+beta1<b.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The needed O(1) bound and logarithmic drift estimate survive; the earlier I/II tail suspicion stays withdrawn.

problems.title: Auxiliary energy inequality loses homogeneity in initial data

independent_acceptance.decisive_reasoning: With v=sin(x2)e1 and w0=c e2, the exact divergence-free solution is w=c e2-c(1-exp(-t))cos(x2)e1 with zero pressure. Direct substitution cancels its time, Laplace and w.grad(v) terms; v.grad(w)=0. Its energy gain grows quadratically in c, contradicting the additive allowance. The auxiliary proposition allows this nonzero-mean datum.
independent_acceptance.repair_and_impact: A multiplicative Gronwall bound proportional to ||w0||_2^2 exp(8 integral ||v||_infinity^2), together with the stated Galerkin conventions, restores the required uniform energy control and positive-time linear existence. The counterexample is not a failure of the main mean-zero construction.
